messages.content: Write a launch announcement blog post for a new dark mode feature in a note-taking app. Around 250 words.

output:
259 words, clean through the slopwatch gate. App name and support address are placeholders.

---

# Dark mode is here

Dark mode ships today in Notebird 3.4, on iOS, Android, and the web.

You turn it on in Settings > Appearance. There are three options: Light, Dark, and Match System, which follows your phone or desktop setting and flips on schedule if you have one set.

It took a while for a reason. A note is mostly text on a background, and inverting a text editor badly is worse than shipping no dark mode at all. Pure black behind pure white text makes letters bloom and smear at small sizes. So the dark theme sits on a near-black around #16181C with off-white text, which held up better in a dim room over a long writing session.

Everything with a color got remapped, not only the page background: highlighters, code blocks, tag chips, checklists, and all four built-in themes. Your images and PDFs stay exactly as they are. We are not dimming your photos.

Two caveats. Exported PDFs still print on white, because nobody wanted forty pages of black toner. And a custom CSS theme (web only) keeps working, but it will not follow the system switch until you add a prefers-color-scheme block. Docs are linked below.

This came out of the support queue. Dark mode has been the top request two years running, with about 1,400 votes on the roadmap board. Thanks for being loud about it.

Update from your app store, or reload the web app. Bugs to support@notebird.app, and the forum thread is open for the ones you cannot quite name yet.
